item.title: Weilenmann School of Discovery introduces new 'PEAK' program - Park Record

item.title: Banksy pieces in Park City prompt call to police encouraging protection of the art - Park Record
item.description: The Park City Police Department received input from someone wanting to ensure the artworks along Main Street created by Banksy years ago are protected.

item.title: Park City No Kings rally set for Saturday - Park Record
item.description: The event will featuring local organizations tabling, speakers, group singing and peaceful marching, organizers said.

item.title: Prodigal peacock finds its way home - Park Record
item.description: Daniel resident Mary Wynne has a sign above her home in Daniel reading, "You can have free food and friends." A blue peacock named Harry Styles was the latest to take up the invitation.

item.title: Take care with route - Park Record
item.description: "I encourage the community to support the development of a cemetery, but not at the cost of creating roadway connections that would significantly alter local traffic patterns."

item.title: Homeowner woes - Park Record
item.description: "We truly prefer to direct our energy and focus on improving the well being and aesthetics of our community and enhancing our quality of life here, not on wasteful legal battles."

item.title: Where are we now? - Park Record
item.description: "Overall, the president’s performance is a mix of a few achievements, but predominantly a list of failures to improve the quality of life for all American citizens."

item.title: Water and Whatever: What the winter that never was suggests - Park Record
item.description: "This winter-that-wasn’t has been a catastrophe for skiers and the local industry, even for Vail Resorts and Alterra, which are somewhat insulated from climate by selling season ski passes in the summer."

item.title: Green Tips: Reusable bags save a lot of plastic or paper at the grocery store - Park Record
item.description: "I used to never bring reusable bags to Trader Joe’s. I’d walk out with four giant paper bags and no plan for what to do with them."

item.title: Where the machine society has led - Park Record
item.description: "As our town continues to grow and modernize, it is worth asking a simple question. Are our systems supporting human life or quietly replacing human contact?"

item.title: Way We Were: Building an exhibit - Park Record
item.description: "The exhibit will help guests discover how our community has come together to celebrate our highest highs, support each other during our lowest lows, and practice solidarity during trying times to stand up for what we believe in."

item.title: How low snowpack could affect the wildfire season this year - Park Record
item.description: "While it is still early to predict wildfire season, in a normal year, we would expect to see more snowstorms before the end of winter. But even if we get several storms, on the current trajectory, it likely won’t fix the problem."

item.title: The Outlook: Epic warmth with glimmers of winter a week away - Park Record
item.description: "If you set foot outside at any point between Tuesday and Saturday of last week, it will come as no surprise that Park City was not spared in this anomalous warmth."

item.title: Ridgelines: Transforming a sport in America - Park Record
item.description: "We’ll miss Diggins’ smile, her spirit, her unmistakable presence on a tour that circles the globe each winter. But her legacy is already moving forward — alive in the next generation of young girls clicking into skis for the first time, and in teammates."
